blocks.title: Who’s who: providers at a glance
blocks.intro: Our SIM-style cards show the facts that matter: whose network a brand really uses, what else it sells and who owns it. Switch between the UK, the USA and Europe.

items.title: BT
items.text: The UK’s former national phone company and one of its biggest broadband providers.

items.title: Sky
items.text: Best known for TV packages; broadband runs over the Openreach network.

items.title: Virgin Media
items.text: Runs its own cable and fibre network instead of Openreach, so availability is address by address.

items.title: O2
items.text: A UK network operator whose masts also carry giffgaff, Tesco Mobile, Sky Mobile and Virgin Mobile.

items.title: giffgaff
items.text: A SIM-only brand with monthly “goodybags” and no long contract, running on O2.

items.title: Smarty
items.text: A SIM-only brand from Three with straightforward data plans, running on the Three network.

items.title: Xfinity
items.text: Comcast’s brand and one of the largest US home internet providers, mostly over cable.

items.title: AT&T
items.text: Runs a national mobile network plus AT&T Fiber and fixed wireless home internet in parts of the country.

items.title: Verizon
items.text: A national mobile carrier that also sells Fios fiber in the Northeast and 5G Home Internet.

items.title: T-Mobile
items.text: A national mobile carrier whose 5G Home Internet is a popular alternative to cable.
specs: 5G Home Internet, fiber in some areas

items.title: Mint Mobile
items.text: Prepaid plans bought in multi-month blocks, running on T-Mobile’s network.

items.title: Starlink
items.text: SpaceX’s low-orbit satellite service, used where cable and fiber don’t reach.

items.title: Deutsche Telekom
items.text: Germany’s largest operator, selling DSL, fibre, MagentaTV and mobile under the Telekom brand.

items.title: Orange
items.text: France’s largest operator, selling fibre with the Livebox router plus mobile plans.

items.title: Free
items.text: Iliad’s French brand, known for Freebox packages and low-cost mobile plans.

items.title: Movistar
items.text: Telefónica’s Spanish brand, with one of Europe’s largest fibre networks.

items.title: TIM
items.text: Italy’s former national telecom operator, selling fibre and mobile.

items.title: KPN
items.text: The Dutch incumbent, with a large fibre roll-out and a mobile network.

blocks.title: How fast can each connection go?
blocks.intro: Every broadband deal sits on one of these technologies. The bars show the typical ceiling of each one, so you can spot a “fibre” deal that isn’t really fibre.

items.title: ADSL (copper)
items.text: The oldest broadband: phone-line copper all the way to your home. Speed falls the further you are from the exchange.

items.title: Part fibre (FTTC / VDSL)
items.text: Fibre to the street cabinet, then copper to your home. Sold as “fibre broadband” in the UK, but it isn’t full fibre.

items.title: 4G / 5G home broadband
items.text: A router with a SIM inside, using a mobile network. No line needed, but speed depends on local signal and busy times.

items.title: Satellite (low orbit)
items.text: Services like Starlink use low-orbit satellites. Useful where nothing else reaches; needs a clear view of the sky.

items.title: Cable (DOCSIS)
items.text: Coaxial cable networks such as Virgin Media, Xfinity and Spectrum. Very fast downloads, slower uploads.

items.title: Full fibre (FTTP / FTTH)
items.text: Fibre optic cable all the way into your home. The fastest and most reliable option, with matching upload speeds on many plans.

blocks.title: Switch in four steps
blocks.intro: In the UK, most broadband and mobile switches are now led by your new provider.

items.title: Check your end date
items.text: Your provider must tell you before your contract ends. Leaving early can mean exit fees.

items.title: Check your address
items.text: Use the provider’s checker and the Ofcom checker for speeds and coverage.

items.title: Read the contract summary
items.text: Price, length, any price rises in pounds and pence, and the minimum speed promised.

items.title: Let the new provider switch you
items.text: One Touch Switch for broadband, or text “PAC” to 65075 to keep your mobile number.

faqs.q: Is FullBars a broadband or mobile provider?
faqs.a: No. FullBars is a free comparison and guide site. You sign up directly with the provider you choose, under their terms. Some links may be affiliate links, which never changes what we write.
We focus on the UK and also cover the USA and Europe, with region guides for US internet and cell plans and European broadband and mobile.

faqs.q: Why don’t you show prices on every card?
faqs.a: Broadband and mobile prices change weekly and vary by address, so a price on a card would quickly be wrong. We show the facts that stay true (network, technology, owner, contract types) and send you to the provider to check today’s price for your address.
Full signal bars: the connection you want. Our job is to help you find a provider that gives you full bars where you live, at a price that makes sense.
